facts.text: Ashland takes its name from the Oregon ash tree that once lined San Lorenzo Creek and the surrounding hills.
Ashland sits in historic Eden Township, bordered by San Leandro to the north, Cherryland to the south, Castro Valley to the east, and San Lorenzo to the southwest.
The Oakland‑San Leandro‑Hayward Electric Railway, built in 1891, ran half‑hourly trains from 5 a.m., with feeder lines from Ashland Junction along Telegraph and Ashland Avenue.
After World War II, cookie‑cutter housing replaced most remaining farms, and Ashland’s primary residential growth occurred during the post‑war period, leaving it largely car‑dependent.
The Nimitz Freeway (I‑880) and I‑238 opened in the late 1950s, cutting through Ashland at Mission Boulevard and continuing to Hesperian Boulevard.
San Lorenzo Creek forms Ashland’s southern edge and is home to the world’s oldest bay tree.
